Hi Liam — following up with the technical detail you asked for and a pointer to a sanitized sample we can share in the call. High-level summary below; happy to deep-dive on any item during the meeting.

Admin activity logs (what we capture)
- Event timestamp (ISO 8601), acting user id, action type (create/update/delete/role-change), target resource id, request id, source IP, agent string, region
- For admin console actions we also capture pre/post change diffs for auditable config changes where relevant

API logs (what we capture)
- Request metadata (endpoint, method, request id, latency), anonymized request/response size, auth token id (hashed), error codes
- We do NOT log raw prompt content or model outputs by default; customers can opt to persist request bodies for debugging under explicit contract and data classification controls

Exportability
- Supported export formats: CSV, JSONL, Parquet. Exports include a signed manifest with checksums per file.
- Exports can be requested via Console or the Admin API; typical export job is delivered to an S3 bucket with presigned URLs for 7 days or pushed to a customer-managed bucket (preferred for audits)

Immutability and audit readiness
- Logs are written to an append-only store with WORM-compatible lifecycle options; we also maintain a time-ordered, signed manifest chain (SHA-256) to provide tamper-evidence for a given retention window
- For customers needing stronger guarantees we offer write-once object storage and periodic notarization (signed timestamps) on exported manifests

Retention and access controls
- Default retention is 13 months for account-level logs; configurable to meet regulatory needs. Access to logs is RBAC-controlled and logged in the same system.

Sanitized sample
- I will bring a sanitized sample CSV and a sample signed manifest to the Tue call. If you prefer to see the sample ahead of time, I can upload a sanitized excerpt to a temporary S3 link.
